variable.name: Chlorophyll-a
variable.long: near-surface chlorophyll-a concentration (satellite estimate, first optical depth)

grid.encoding: zlib-deflated uint16 as two byte planes (all low bytes, then all high bytes); q = 0 no data (land, ice, persistent cloud or polar night); log10(chl mg/m^3) = lo + (q - 1) * step
grid.aggregation: 3 x 3 block mean of log10(chlor_a) from the 9 km grid (>= 3 valid pixels of 9)

caveats: Satellite chlorophyll is an estimate from ocean colour, not a measurement in the water; uncertainty is about 30-35 % in the open ocean and larger in coastal water, where sediment and dissolved organic matter (rivers, Baltic, Black Sea, Rio de la Plata) make it read too high.
It sees only the top optical depth (roughly 10-60 m); deep chlorophyll maxima in the gyres are invisible.
High latitudes have no data in their winter (polar night, sea ice), so a monthly map has seasonal holes and the annual (CU) layer is biased towards the sunlit season there.
Monthly climatologies start in different years (the mission started in July 2002): see layers[].period.
